item.expandedweather2dynamics.handheld_a: A hand anemometer: the wind where you are standing, the bearing it is coming from, and the highest gust it has seen since you last cleared it.
item.expandedweather2dynamics.handheld.u: Right-click to read, sneak-use to clear the peak. Needs open sky.
item.expandedweather2dynamics.handheld_t: A pocket thermometer: the air's temperature on this mod's own scale, less the lapse with height, so a summit reads colder than the plain below it.
item.expandedweather2dynamics.handheld.u: Right-click to read. Reads anywhere, indoors included.
item.expandedweather2dynamics.handheld_b: A pocket barometer: station pressure, its band, and the tendency the device's own last two readings give - which is the half of a barometer that predicts anything.
item.expandedweather2dynamics.handheld.u: Right-click to read; read it twice to get a tendency.
item.expandedweather2dynamics.camera.too: Right-click to photograph the storm you are aiming at. Scored on framing, distance, how much of it is visible, the structure above it, the light and the foreground.
Sneak and right-click to open the album.
item.expandedweather2dynamics.spotter_fl: Fired at a funnel to file a tornado report. Sirens in range sound, villagers shelter, and the world will prove you right or not.

advancements.expandedweather2dynamics.cy: Record cycloidal marks after a tornado.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.s: The short version: how often storms come, how many there are at once, how big and how violent they get, how hard it rains, and whether they may break anything. Each of these scales the detailed settings below rather than replacing them, so at the default nothing here changes the mod as it was tuned.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.g: A tornado forms in real time: organizing wall cloud, then the condensation descending while a dust whirl turns below it, then touchdown, then widening to full strength.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.s: The mod's own storm structure: Weather2's timer-driven staging is paced here instead, so a storm is held on each rung before it may climb. Because the windfield reads the rung, this is also half of keeping a tornado from reaching damaging wind the instant it is labelled tornadic. Storms driven by the command, a weather machine, a player or another feature are exempt.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.r: A storm's rain drawn as a volume by a shader rather than as stacks of billboard sheets, from the same field that shapes the hook and the clear slot - so a curtain of rain between you and a tornado hides the tornado.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.m: How a violent tornado embeds smaller vortices in its own circulation. A ground swarm is the arrangement where the parent barely touches the ground and the sub-vortices do the damage.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.s: A strong tornado tears a whole building off its foundation and breaks it apart in the air, instead of only nibbling the loose blocks out of it. With whole-building lift on, the building comes away entire, tumbles around the funnel, and then sheds its blocks from the outside in.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.h: The three handheld instruments: an anemometer that reports the wind where you are standing and remembers its own peak gust, a thermometer that reports the air on a stated scale with height, and a barometer that reports the column and the tendency its own last reading gives. Every one of them is the same reading the block instrument beside it takes, asked from wherever the holder is standing, so the two cannot disagree.
How long a handheld instrument takes to settle between readings, in ticks (20 = one second). A reading is a message in the chat, so this is what stops holding the button from filling it.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.s: Whether weather instruments can be wired back to a weather computer with the mod's own cable, so the computer reports the network rather than only the air at its own four walls. An instrument within a block of any wire on the run is on the network, and a complete network is one of each of the three readings.

How many wire blocks the walk from a weather computer to its instruments may cross. A cable is meant to run across a base, not across a province: past this length the instruments are not on the network.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.r: Whether obsidian reinforced glass resists what ordinary glass does not: the wind, the hail and the derecho's roof pass all refuse it, exactly as they refuse bedrock. Off leaves it an ordinary pane with an expensive recipe.

Whether structural rebars anchor what they are driven into. A planted rebar protects itself and the blocks around it from being pulled out, lifted or stripped, which is what turns a roof into something a player can hold on with. A rebar with nothing under it anchors nothing.
How many blocks above a rebar the anchoring reaches. A rebar is driven in at the bottom of what it holds: at 3 it holds a wall three blocks tall around it.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.m: Whether a village weather station gives a villager the meteorologist profession: a villager who claims the station and trades in what the sky leaves behind - storm-log paper and sensor parts in, instruments and supplies out. Off leaves the block a decoration with no job attached.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.s: A landspout or waterspout takes what a strong gust takes: leaves off the trees, carpets off the floor, torches and flowers and crops off the ground. This is the tier below a tornado and it is meant to stay survivable - a spout never touches soil, stone, planks or logs, and it never digs. Off returns the old behaviour, where a spout under 62 mph was decoration.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.b: A wildfire leaves the ground it has been over: the canopy burned away, some trunks left standing as charred spars, bare earth where the litter was. The scar follows the fire's own track rather than appearing in a ring around it, so the pass has a direction by the time the fire has walked a few hundred blocks.

Whether a wildfire leaves trunks standing as charred wood. Off burns the canopy and scorches the ground but leaves every trunk where it stood, for a world that wants the scar without the changed timber.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.h: What the ice does when it lands: crops knocked down, canopy stripped, thin glass broken, farmland beaten flat, and anything caught in the open hit by whatever size is falling.
Hailstones land on things. The mod has always grown a hail core and drawn its shaft; this is the ice itself arriving. Off leaves hail exactly as it was - a reading the sky and the renderer use.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.c: Hail that lands on things makes a sound, in the material it landed on: a wooden roof rattles, a stone one ticks, a metal one rings, a glass one pings, and the grass around you patters. The surface is read off the block's own sound type, so a roof made of any block still sounds like what it is made of, and what you hear is the stones hitting the things around you.

How far around a player the stones are listened for, in blocks. A strike inside this radius is played where it happened and fades with distance, which is what puts the roof over your head in front of the barn across the field. It is a ceiling rather than the whole answer: the size of the stones caps it, because a pea's clatter is not worth chasing across a field and a baseball's is.

Multiplier on every piece of hail clatter. 1 is the mod's own mix - a baseball on a metal roof is loud and a pea in a field is barely there - and above 1 is for a world that wants the storm to fill the room.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.h: How much of a hailstrike a helmet takes off. Protection rather than immunity on purpose: at the default of 0.65 a baseball still hurts through an iron helmet.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.d: Multiplier on every hailstrike's damage. Hail is the one hazard in this mod that can hit a player who is doing nothing wrong in a field, so this is the dial for a world that wants the stones to sting rather than to kill.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.l: The little spirals of leaves a gust front lifts off the ground before its storm arrives - the first thing anybody sees of an approaching outflow, minutes before the rain. Client-side only.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.s: How far a squall line has to travel before it counts as a derecho. SPC's criterion is a 400 km damage swath, which is larger than any world here, so this is that shape rescaled to the distances a line in this mod can actually cover.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.t: Whether a derecho lays standing trunks down along its swath: the trunk goes over and its logs lie on the ground downwind of the stump, which is what a combed forest looks like afterwards.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.r: Whether a derecho takes weak roof covering - shingles, planks, slabs, panes, carpet - off a building and leaves the walls standing. Stone, brick and metal are never touched.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.f: How much harder rain floods at the peak of the wet season, where the ground has been wet for days instead of soaking it in.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.s: How much of the sky the season takes at its peak, as a share of the mod's own storm tint. A wet season is grey rather than black.
How freely a lava whirl spills lava, as a multiplier on its own odds. 0 leaves the whirl burning what it crosses without ever changing the ground under it.

Whether a steam devil scalds anything standing inside it. Steam is hot and has no mass, so this is a burn and never a block: a steam devil cannot move a wall, and one that did would be a different phenomenon.

The world's own year: the day counted from the world's clock, what each season does to the air, and the month multipliers and datapack day windows a pack uses to say which parts of the year are the dangerous ones.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.t: The ground a land tornado may be born over. A biome that reads as plains country, or that a pack has listed in the tornado genesis biome tag, is allowed; anything else refuses the genesis. Whirls and waterspouts belong to their own country and are unaffected.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.d: Whether a day can carry a deadly storm. Weather2 promotes a freshly formed storm into a deadly one every three game days, or ten on its land-based timer, and only asks one question first: whether the cell that formed may be deadly. This section is that question, answered from the air - instability gates it and shear shapes it - and it is the same reading the forecast prints, so the percentage in the readout and the storms the world actually gets cannot disagree.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.e: Draw The Eclipse Under A Shaderpack
Extend Fog To The LOD Distance
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.p: How far a portable radar reaches for a weather radar to link to. The handheld shows the nearest weather radar block's own product, range and live returns, and only sweeps from the player's own position when no weather radar is within this distance.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.t: Width surges layered over the dynamic width. 0 holds the calm curve; higher swings the funnel further. The width arrives at a new value and holds it for a minute or two instead of swelling and shrinking on a beat, and each storm draws its own values.
Legacy multiplier used only when Realistic Width Model is off. This value is not miles.
Legacy multiplier used only when Realistic Width Model is off. This value is not miles.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.m: Set to 5.0 for five miles, which converts to about 8047 blocks. Set to 0 to use Max Damage Width (Blocks).
Optional rendered funnel cap in miles. Leave at 0 for the survival-friendly block cap.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.r: Damage Surveyor ignores tracks without recent points, so old tornadoes do not get picked by new surveys.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.a: Rare natural tornadoes can rotate opposite the normal Weather2 spin using StormObject.spinSpeed.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.w: Scales Weather2 tornado visual spin from addon windfield mph without changing damage or pull strength.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.e: Lets narrow or moderate tornadoes use a curved elephant-trunk funnel morphology without renaming the tornado or changing damage physics.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.d: Lets rare tornadoes lock into a narrow drill-bit funnel with faster visual spin and slightly punchier dynamic wind.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.s: Visual-only stick item particles in vortices and straight-line wind. These are not dropped items.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.m: Client-side cap for all stick debris particles per tick.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.t: Uses Weather2 cloud256 particles tinted dark brown to create a visual-only debris/dust cloud around tornado ground circulations.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.m: Client-side cap for large dark-brown tornado debris cloud particles.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.f: Sways leaves and grass in the terrain vertex shader using local Weather2 storm wind. Visual only.
When Physics Mod is installed, uses its local wind domain and leaves Physics Mod-managed vines alone.
Maximum foliage vertex displacement in blocks. Keep low for subtle motion and shader-pack safety.
Wind speed where foliage reaches full sway/thrash intensity.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.w: Adds a lowered rotating wall cloud under the supercell rain-free updraft base.

Persistent rotating wall clouds can modestly increase the radar's tornado potential, but they do not trigger TOR warnings alone. The SPC outlook is a forecast of the environment and is never moved by observed storm structure, so this affects the radar only.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.f: How the areas on a forecast display's plate are drawn: cut to the scope rather than pinned to its rim, laid down from the broadest category to the tightest so the bands nest, hatched where a hazard is significant, and outlined with a soft halo.

How solid the outlook's areas are. This is a tint by default: the nesting is read from each category's outline, which gains alpha and width as this comes down, so the plate stays an instrument surface rather than becoming the outlook's own green. Raise it towards 1 for flat map colours.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.h: Hatch the significant-hazard areas - the greatest tornado risk, the 2 inch hail risk, an outbreak setup - the way a real outlook hatches them instead of drawing another outline. Off leaves only the dashed outline.
Distance between the hatch lines, in plate units, where the whole plate is about three. Fine enough not to read as stripes, coarse enough to see from a few blocks away.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.c: Mark the corners a warning polygon actually turns at, the way warnings are drawn on a real display. Watches are left unmarked, since the dash is what tells them apart.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.f: The lines under a forecast display's map, and the panel they stand on.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.r: Stand the readout on a panel that turns to face you, instead of printing it flat on the plate. The plate stays a map - outlook areas, warnings and storms are read by looking down at them - but text in that plane is squashed by the angle you read it from and is only legible from directly overhead. Off prints the same lines flat, as the display did before.

How big to set that panel, against the size the mod works out from how far away you are. The mod grows it with distance so it stays about the same size on screen out to fourteen blocks and then shrinks away; this multiplies that, so you can have it readable from further off, or half the size if a hologram over the block is not for you.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.v: A villager that has got itself under a roof shuts the doors it can reach, and reaches further the closer the funnel is. Only ever closes doors, never opens them, and only once the villager is inside.
A frightened villager makes a noise while it is out in the open, faster and higher as the funnel closes, and goes quiet once it is under a roof.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.a: Herd animals react to a funnel the way cattle do: they bunch up and the bunch drifts out of the funnel's way, across its track rather than down it. Water animals and tamed animals are left alone.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.i: Optional reflection-only Immersive Vehicles/MTS storm physics. Inactive unless MTS is installed.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.s: Dense rain cores and strong tornado inflow can stall MTS engines by reducing safe engine fields.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.o: Open-top MTS seats can lose riders only under strong tornado suction.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.t: Optional reflection-only Tree Physics compat. Falling tree sublevels can be dragged, lifted, and thrown by active storm windfields.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.s: High-energy thrown Tree Physics trunks can punch through fragile or residential blocks with strict per-tick caps.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.r: Loops a low tornado roar near active tornado circulations.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.c: Adds subtle wind-pressure camera motion near dangerous tornado windfields.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.i: Uses a GLSL shader pass for inflow streaks, dust veil, and core ring effects inside the tornado damage path.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.e: Briefly clears and muffles the innermost core while keeping a rotating fog wall at the edges.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.w: Whites the screen out whenever you are inside a tornado funnel: fog collapses to a few blocks, the fog colour goes to dusty grey, and a flat dust veil covers the view. Ramps in from the funnel wall and saturates in the core. Works independently of the inside-core effects and of the opt-in inflow shader.
How few blocks away the fog closes in completely at full whiteout. Lower is a thicker wall of dust.

Where the whiteout begins, as a multiple of the funnel wall radius (the radius of maximum wind). 1.0 starts it at the wall; below 1.0 keeps it to the inner core, above 1.0 closes in before you are engulfed.
Opacity of the flat dust veil at full whiteout. 1.0 hides everything; 0.0 leaves only the fog.

How much debris the whiteout veil carries: dust streaks tearing past, dark clumps of boards and sheet metal crossing the view, and a fine grit over the whole veil. All three scale with how violent the funnel is, so an EF1 is murk you can half see through and an EF4 is a brownout. 0.0 restores the plain flat veil.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.b: Adds close-core saturation, pitch wobble, and low rumble to the tornado roar.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.c: Maximum radius for close tornado roar and camera shake. Default 30 blocks keeps these effects local to the tornado.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.a: Reduces camera/FOV motion while keeping audio, fog, and debris cues.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.t: How much the track's forward speed varies over the tornado's life. The storm crawls while the mesocyclone cycles, then lunges forward; 0 holds one steady pace. Applied before the speed floor and ceiling, so a tornado can never leave the honest 6-34 mph band. Weak and rope funnels surge hardest; violent wedges stay steadier.
Slowest a tornado track may translate, in miles per hour. Real slow movers still crawl forward; 6 mph is a realistic floor.
Fastest a tornado track may translate, in miles per hour. Real tornadoes essentially never exceed 40 mph; Joplin averaged about 30 mph over its 22 mile path.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.i: How much a violent tornado is slowed below the ambient flow speed. Strong tornadoes are deviant and slower than the wind carrying them; 0 keeps every tornado at flow speed.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.t: How much rough or hilly terrain bleeds off track speed, up to the roughness penalty. Real tornadoes slow slightly crossing broken terrain.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.m: Curvature limit for the track, in degrees per tick. 0.18 is about 3.6 degrees per second: enough for smooth long arcs while making a kinked or snapped heading impossible. Weak and rope tornadoes may turn faster than violent wedges.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.d: Extra clockwise, right-of-motion veer at full intensity, on top of the right-of-flow bias. Deviant motion is strongest on violent tornadoes - an EF5 can run 30 degrees right of the mean flow - and fades to nothing on weak ones.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.s: Player-filed tornado reports: what counts as reportable, how long a report stands, and what a confirmed one pays.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.w: Launchable radiosonde: ascends, radios temperature, dewpoint, pressure and wind back to the launcher, reports nearby storms, then parachutes its package home.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.o: Reissues the outlook on the SPC schedule through the day, each issue re-examining the environment with a diurnal heating curve, so an outlook can be upgraded in the afternoon and downgraded overnight. Off issues one outlook per day at dawn.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.g: Brief shallow vortices along thunderstorm outflow boundaries. They show on radar/forecaster but are not tornado warnings by themselves.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.h: Broad maritime tropical-cyclone-style storm complexes derived from Weather2 storms in late-season ocean conditions.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.f: Capped shallow flood water under heavy Weather2 rain cores, squall lines, and hurricanes. It is loaded-chunk only.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.e: Uses Weather2/ExtendedRenderer EntityRotFX particles for addon storm visuals, debris clouds, distant downfall, and close tornado effects.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.s: Darken the sky, the fog, the cloud deck and the world's own ambient light under a storm's mass, from this mod's own reading of that mass rather than by driving the game's rain state. The sun, the moon and the stars are hidden by the same number. Off leaves every one of those exactly as the game drew it.
How far into that darkening a storm goes. 1.0 lets a direct hit with a hailing core reach the game's own midnight, 0.5 tops out halfway there, 0 leaves the shapes and takes none of the light.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.h: A green sky over a hailing cell. The sky turns green only where stones are falling around you or over a hail core in sight, gated on the same size ladder as the hail itself, with nothing below quarter-sized stones.
How green the sky goes at the middle of a baseball-sized hail core. 1 is the mod's own mix - muted, so it reads as weather rather than as a filter - and 0 is the same as switching the green off.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.a: Steers Weather2 tornado motion from the global wind grid with an ENE/right-of-flow bias. It does not alter tornado width or damage physics.
Legacy option kept for old configs. Global-wind steering now stays strict and does not add stochastic wobble.
expandedweather2dynamics.configuration.d: Fictional in-game SPC-style outlook issued as real SPC products: probability contours and conditional intensity groups (hatching) per hazard on the 0600Z/1300Z/1630Z/2000Z/0100Z cycle, with the risk category derived from the SPC probability-to-categorical decision matrix. Past the published high risk the ladder continues onto the extreme and hyper extreme tiers, which are reachable through conditional intensity groups 4 and 5 (an EF5 tornado, a 130 mph derecho gust, or a near-ceiling environment) and carry an extra spawn push. It controls storm spawn probabilities only, not active tornado lifecycle or width.
